- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model overpredicts; reduce forecast to reflect bearish sentiment.  
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5–10% in 1–2 days); apply a 1–2 day lag correction to smooth out overreaction.  
- Forecast mean reverts too quickly after strong moves; extend mean reversion window to 3–5 days for smoother transitions.  
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates late-period price action (last 7–10 days); adjust downward by 1–3% for final 10 days if sentiment remains neutral or slightly bullish.  
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-period, model fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” rule: reduce forecast slope by 10–20% after sentiment drops below 0.5.
